_note:
ISOLDE KERROW, who directs the Stillwater Concord: the small, old, regional survey body that has measured this coast for sixty years and is currently losing eleven of its fifteen staff to the Meridian Foundation.

WHY THE SCENE IS HERE. The player meets Cassian Veyl in the next town, and CANON is explicit that he must not read as a villain -- his argument is genuinely reasonable and the player should half want to trust him. That lands about four times harder if somebody has already made the same argument, honestly, out of real grief, one map earlier, with no money and no power and nothing to gain by it. Kerrow is that person. She is not Meridian, she is not against them, and she is not a plant; she is a woman who lost a brother to a storm and cannot afford the thing she watches them doing.

She does NOT tell the player what to think. She tells them what she wants and admits she cannot have it.

lines: {name}. You are the one filling in a Vellum for Halcyon Sorrell.
Isolde Kerrow. I direct the Stillwater Concord, which this year mostly means signing leaving papers.
Eleven of fifteen. All to the Foundation. I signed every one and I meant every good word in them.
Seventy years ago the sea came over this coast in one night and took a town called Old Tidefall.
Two hundred and forty people. My brother was one of them. I was six.
So you can guess what I want. I want it never to happen again.
Not survived. Not recorded. Stopped.
And out there on that ridge is an organisation with the money to try.
New instruments beside four of my stations. Better than mine. Warmer coats than mine.
You want me to tell you they are wrong. I have been sitting in this chair failing to.
She has not looked away from you once.
I do not know. That is the honest answer and I hate the sound of it.
Two hundred and eleven core samples out from under Stonewake. Forty crates over the ridge.
None of it near the water, and every bit of it going to the water.
I have. Twice, in writing. Both times I got a courteous answer inside a week.
Courteous, complete, and about something slightly to the left of what I asked.
You cannot put that in a report. I have tried to draft it four times.
Go on down to Tideglass. Take your Crest, they are a fine thing to have.
Dr Veyl speaks in the square there this season, and you should go and hear him.
You will like him. Everybody does. Do not let that be the end of your thinking about it.
The Director's chair is empty. The soundings pinned above it are not.
Somebody has ringed the same stretch of the ridge road twice, and written one word beside it.
The word is WHY, and it has been gone over so many times it has torn the paper.
